conventions.convention: Population values are fixed; design probability randomizes the sampled subset. The diagonal inclusion convention is πii = πi.
Δij = πij − πiπj for ordered pairs, including Δii = πi(1 − πi).
SRSWOR uses all n-element subsets with equal mass 1/binomial(N,n), for integers 1 ≤ n ≤ N.
The variance identity requires positive first-order inclusion probabilities; the all-pairs inverse-inclusion estimate additionally requires πij > 0 for every ordered pair.
The SYG identity assumes fixed sample size. Nonpositive distinct-pair Δij is sufficient for nonnegative sample estimates, rather than necessary for a particular fixed population.
S_U² uses denominator N − 1 and requires N > 1; the sample-mean variance formula allows n = 1 and n = N.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite population and sampling design with πi > 0 for every unit, Var_d(T̂_HT) = Σi,j Δij yi yj/(πiπj). If additionally πij > 0 for every ordered pair, V̂_HT = Σi,j IiIj(Δij/πij)(yi/πi)(yj/πj) is defined and has expectation Var_d(T̂_HT).
For SRSWOR with N > 1 and 1 ≤ n ≤ N, Cov_d(Ii,Ij) = −n(N−n)/(N²(N−1)) for distinct units, and Var_d(ȳ_S) = (1−n/N)S_U²/n. Both formulas include n = 1 and n = N.

For a fixed-size sampling design with πi > 0 and xi = yi/πi, Σj Δij = 0 and Var_d(T̂_HT) = −(1/2)Σi,j Δij(xi−xj)². Under positive inclusion probabilities for every ordered pair, the inverse-pair sample expression is unbiased; Δij ≤ 0 for distinct pairs guarantees its nonnegativity on every supported sample.
For an integer n with 1 ≤ n ≤ N, SRSWOR of size n has support {s ⊆ U : |s| = n} and assigns every supported sample probability 1/binomial(N,n).
For each ordered pair (i,j) ∈ U × U, Δij := πij − πiπj; the convention πii = πi gives Δii = πi(1−πi).

seams_checked.note: The variance page preserves fixed population values, finite design support, observed inclusion indicators, and πii = πi. Positive first-order and pair-inclusion hypotheses are added explicitly where required.

The stratified definition uses independent uniform fixed-size samples. The variance theorem quotes the SRSWOR formula with N > 1 and applies it only to noncertainty strata, where Nh > 1 follows from 1 ≤ nh < Nh. Certainty strata, including singleton strata, are handled directly as constants.
